# ======================================:
# ========================================
# WebRPA Python Script Module - Tutorial
# ========================================

# 1. Accessing Workflow Variables
# ----------------------------------------
# The system automatically injects all workflow variables; access them directly via vars.<name>
# For example:
# - vars.username  # Get the username variable
# - vars.count     # Get the count variable
# - vars.items     # Get the items list variable
# - vars.user_info # Get the user_info dict variable

# If a variable does not exist, use the get() method to provide a default value
# username = vars.get('username', 'default user')
# age = vars.get('age', 0)

# View all available variables
print(f"All available variables: {list(vars.keys())}")


# 2. Writing Your Business Logic
# ----------------------------------------
# Example 1: simple calculation
result = 1 + 1
print(f"Calculation result: {result}")

# Example 2: using a workflow variable
# Assume the workflow has a variable named 'name'
if 'name' in vars.keys():
    name = vars.name  # or vars.get('name')
    greeting = f"Hello, {name}!"
    print(greeting)

# Example 3: processing list data
# Assume the workflow has a list variable named 'numbers'
if 'numbers' in vars.keys():
    numbers = vars.numbers
    total = sum(numbers)
    print(f"Sum of numbers: {total}")


# 3. Returning Results to the Workflow
# ----------------------------------------
# Simply use return to return a result
# Any type is supported: string, number, list, dict, etc.

# Example: returning a dict
output_data = {
    'status': 'success',
    'result': result,
    'message': 'Processing complete'
}

# Return directly (the system automatically saves it to the specified return-value variable)
return output_data


# ========================================
# Tips
# ========================================
# 1. Accessing variables: use vars.<name> or vars.get('<name>', default)
#    The system automatically injects all workflow variables, no manual configuration needed
#
# 2. Return value: use return to return data of any type
#    Specify the receiving variable name in the "Return Value Variable" field of the config panel
#    For example: result, which can then be referenced with {result}
#
# 3. Standard output: the content of print() is saved to the "Standard Output Variable" (if configured)
#
# 4. Built-in libraries: you can use all standard libraries of Python 3.13
#    as well as the third-party libraries built into WebRPA (requests, pandas, etc.)
#
# 5. Easy to use: just like writing a regular Python script, no complex configuration needed
# ========================================
